pr.title: Always inline functions signatures containing `f16` or `f128`
pr.description:
There are a handful of tier 2 and tier 3 targets that cause a LLVM crash or linker error when generating code that contains `f16` or `f128`. The cranelift backend also does not support these types. To work around this, every function in `std` or `core` that contains these types must be marked `#[inline]` in order to avoid sending any code to the backend unless specifically requested.

However, this is inconvenient and easy to forget. Introduce a check for these types in the frontend that automatically inlines any function signatures that take or return `f16` or `f128`.

Note that this is not a perfect fix because it does not account for the types being passed by reference or as members of aggregate types, but this is sufficient for what is currently needed in the standard library.

Fixes: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/133035
Closes: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/133037
pr.author: tgross35

classification.name: Inline
evidence: The patch changes the `cross_crate_inlinable` query to force cross-crate inlining eligibility for signatures containing `f16`/`f128`. This query is consumed by the concrete `Inline` MIR pass: `impl<'tcx> crate::MirPass<'tcx> for Inline` feeds `self.tcx.cross_crate_inlinable(...)` into `check_codegen_attributes`, where a non-generic callee is rejected unless cross-crate inlinable. The same query also affects codegen instantiation decisions, but that is not a separate MirPass; no other pass implementation is directly justified by this change.

processing.reason: The historical change is a compiler inlining-policy/codegen workaround, not a runtime semantic transformation. Forcing `cross_crate_inlinable` to return true for direct `f16`/`f128` signatures changes whether such functions are emitted to the backend; the actual regression test is a codegen `CHECK-NOT` test with unused `todo!()` functions and no runtime execution. On a backend that supports these types, inlined and non-inlined calls have identical defined values; on an unsupported backend the pre-fix behavior can crash or fail to link, not produce a different executable result. Therefore no source-grounded pair of ordinary Rust functions can both pass Miri and produce different deterministic runtime values. Modeling the internal query with a different boolean return would only test a reimplementation of compiler internals, not the historical program semantics, so it would be an artificial counterexample rather than the actual regression.

analysis.originalLogic: `cross_crate_inlinable` began by checking the function's definition/attributes and then applied its normal cross-crate-inlining policy, including an incremental-compilation early exit. It did not inspect the function signature for `f16`/`f128`, so such functions remained ordinarily non-cross-crate-inlinable. The `Inline` MIR pass consumes this query for callee inlining decisions and can reject inlining a non-generic callee.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect behavior was to classify functions whose direct inputs or output are exactly `f16` or `f128` as ordinary, non-forced-inlining functions. Consequently, when such a function was not otherwise inlined (for example at a low optimization level or when cross-crate inlining was disabled), backend code generation could receive unsupported `f16`/`f128` signatures and crash or fail at link time. The fix is to force the `cross_crate_inlinable` query to return `true` immediately when any direct signature input or the output equals `tcx.types.f16` or `tcx.types.f128`: `if ty == &tcx.types.f16 || ty == &tcx.types.f128 { return true; }`. This is not a claim that a different deliberate rewrite was executed; it is the absence of this forced-inline classification.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust MIR functions whose signature directly takes or returns `f16` or `f128` by value, as tested by `pub fn f16_arg(_a: f16)`, `pub fn f16_ret() -> f16`, `pub fn f128_arg(_a: f128)`, and `pub fn f128_ret() -> f128`. The PR explicitly limits coverage: it does not account for these types passed by reference or embedded in aggregate types.
analysis.summary: Force `cross_crate_inlinable` to return true when a function signature directly contains `f16` or `f128`, so the `Inline` MIR pass does not leave such functions for backend code generation on targets/backends lacking support. The regression test disables optimization and cross-crate inlining and verifies the `f16`/`f128` functions are not emitted.
analysis.trigger: Compiling `std`/`core` or a user crate containing direct `f16`/`f128` argument or return types on a tier 2/tier 3 target or backend that crashes or errors when generating code for those types, especially when normal optimization/inlining would not otherwise remove the function.
preconditions: The function signature directly contains `f16` or `f128` in an input or in the output; references and aggregates are outside this fix's scope.
The function would otherwise not be inlined, such as with `-Copt-level=0`, `-Zcross-crate-inline-threshold=never`, `-Zmir-opt-level=0`, and `-Cno-prepopulate-passes`.
The backend or target lacks support for `f16`/`f128`, so emitting the function can cause an LLVM crash or linker error.
pitfalls: Returning true only after the normal incremental-compilation early exit would miss the forced-inline case; the new check is placed before that early exit.
Checking only one input or only the return type is insufficient: the test covers both argument and return positions for both types.
The fix intentionally does not cover `f16`/`f128` behind references or inside aggregate types, so tests should not infer support for those cases.

Passing these values by reference was previously used as a workaround in `core`; the patch changes `min`/`max` assertion arguments from `&f16`/`&f128` to by-value `f16`/`f128`, exercising the new guarantee.
A codegen test using only optimized settings could pass because ordinary inlining removes the functions; the regression test includes a no-optimization revision.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a codegen test with two revisions: `default`, and `nopt` using `-Copt-level=0 -Zcross-crate-inline-threshold=never -Zmir-opt-level=0 -Cno-prepopulate-passes`. Define `pub` functions taking and returning `f16` and `f128`, and assert `CHECK-NOT: f16_arg`, `CHECK-NOT: f16_ret`, `CHECK-NOT: f128_arg`, and `CHECK-NOT: f128_ret` so unsupported signatures are not emitted. Also exercise the library path by changing `f16::clamp`/`f128::clamp` assertion arguments from references to by-value values. Do not claim runtime execution or reproduction; these are compile/codegen checks.
